lesson.text: Quick memory: how many degrees are there in a right angle, and in a full turn? (90° and 360°.) In grade 4 you measured angles with a protractor. Now you will work them out without measuring, with angle facts.
Angles on a straight line add up to 180°, half a turn. If one of two angles on a line is 130°, the other is 180 − 130 = 50°.
Angles round a point add up to 360°, a full turn. Here 100° and 120° and 140° make 360° together. To find a missing angle, take the others away from 360°.
When two straight lines cross, they make four angles. The angles opposite each other are vertically opposite angles, and they are always equal. Angles next to each other lie on a straight line: 180°.
The three angles inside any triangle add up to 180°. Tear the three corners off a paper triangle and put them side by side: they make a straight line! Here 60°, 70° and 50° make 180°.

A worked example: a triangle has a right angle (the small square) and a 35° angle. The third angle is 180 − 90 − 35 = 55°. In an isosceles triangle two sides are equal, and so are two angles. An equilateral triangle's angles are all 60°.
The four angles inside any quadrilateral add up to 360°: a diagonal cuts it into two triangles, and 2 × 180 = 360. In a parallelogram, opposite angles are equal.

Try it in the world: draw a four-sided shape on paper, cut it out, tear off its four corners and fit them round a point: they make a full turn. Next, in grade 6: the area of triangles; in grade 7: more angle facts.

exercises.prompt: The angles are on a straight line. What is the missing angle, in degrees?
exercises.hint: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°.

exercises.prompt: The angles in a triangle always add up to 180°.
exercises.hint: Remember the torn-off corners that made a straight line.
exercises.explain: True: every triangle, big or small, has angles that add up to 180°.

exercises.prompt: What do the angles round a point add up to?
exercises.explain: The angles round a point make a full turn: 360°.

exercises.prompt: The lines cross. What is the angle opposite the 70° angle, in degrees?
exercises.hint: Vertically opposite angles face each other across the crossing.

exercises.prompt: What do the angles inside a quadrilateral add up to?
exercises.hint: A diagonal cuts it into two triangles.

exercises.prompt: What is the missing angle in this triangle, in degrees?
exercises.hint: Take the two angles you know away from 180°.

exercises.prompt: The angles are round a point, and one is a right angle. What is the angle marked ?, in degrees?
exercises.hint: A right angle is 90°. All the angles round a point add up to 360°.

exercises.prompt: This quadrilateral has two right angles. What is the angle marked ?, in degrees?
exercises.hint: The four angles add up to 360°. Each right angle is 90°.

exercises.prompt: Sort them: could these be the three angles of a triangle?
exercises.hint: Add the three angles. A triangle's angles make exactly 180°.

exercises.prompt: A triangle can have two obtuse angles (each more than 90°).
exercises.hint: What do two angles of more than 90° add up to?
exercises.explain: False: two obtuse angles already make more than 180°, and a triangle's three angles make exactly 180°.

exercises.prompt: One angle on the straight line is a right angle. What is the angle marked ?, in degrees?
exercises.hint: The right angle is 90°. The three angles make 180°.

exercises.prompt: Put the steps in order to find a triangle's third angle when two are 40° and 75°.
exercises.hint: First find how much of the 180° is already used.

exercises.prompt: This isosceles triangle has two equal sides, marked. What is the angle marked ?, in degrees?
exercises.hint: The two angles at the bottom are equal. First take 40° away from 180°.
exercises.explain: 180 − 40 = 140, and the two equal angles share it: 140 ÷ 2 = 70°.

exercises.prompt: This quadrilateral is a parallelogram. What is the angle marked ?, in degrees?
exercises.hint: Angles next to each other in a parallelogram add up to 180°.
exercises.explain: Next to each other, they make 180°: 180 − 65 = 115°. So the angles are 65°, 115°, 65° and 115°: 360°.

exercises.prompt: Which two angles are vertically opposite?
exercises.hint: Vertically opposite angles face each other across the crossing point.
exercises.explain: a and c face each other across the point (so do b and d), so they are equal.

exercises.prompt: An equilateral triangle has three angles of 60°.
exercises.hint: Its three angles are equal and add up to 180°.

exercises.prompt: Two angles of a quadrilateral are 100° each. The other two are equal to each other. What is each of them, in degrees?
exercises.hint: Take the two angles you know from 360°, then share what is left between the two equal angles.

exercises.prompt: A triangle has angles of 90°, 45° and 45°. What kind of triangle is it?
exercises.hint: Look for a 90° angle, and for two angles that are the same.
exercises.explain: It has a right angle, and two equal angles (so two equal sides): right-angled and isosceles.
